Java: Align code with project standard
commitResults.messageBody:
Java sources use the default package and contain inconsistent naming,
documentation, and formatting. This makes the project harder to navigate
and prevents it from following the required SE-EDU conventions.

Move the chatbot classes into the lokwx package and align their
Javadocs, identifiers, switch handling, and whitespace with the project
standard. Update the README source path so the application remains easy
to launch.

Java changes need a durable project-specific standard so future work
follows the same SE-EDU conventions.

Add a repository skill that records the Java rules and require agents
to apply it whenever creating or reviewing Java code.

Commit messages and branch names need a consistent project convention.

Add a repository skill based on the SE-EDU Git rules and require agents
to apply it to future commits and branches.

commitResults.messageBody:
Categorize tasks into Todo, Deadline, and Event types to
support task-specific display messages.

Extend task tracking to distinguish todos, deadlines, and events so each
task retains the scheduling information relevant to its type.
- Represent todos as tasks without date or time information.
- Store and display the due date or time for deadlines.
- Store and display the start and end times for events.
- Add type markers and use type-specific formatting when adding or
  listing tasks.
- Report the updated task count after each addition.

commitResults.messageBody:
Add a test-ui skill that records command and expected-output pairs,
preserves console transcripts, and stops on the first failure.

Require agents to review the UI test plan and invoke the skill after each
code update so console behavior is checked consistently.

TaskHandler stores tasks in an instance-owned array, but a static count
shares its position across all handlers. Creating a second handler can
therefore index its empty array using another handler's state, causing gaps
or null access.

Give each handler its own count and instance getter so the count and task
array share the same lifetime and scope. This follows the guideline to
minimize variable scope and removes hidden coupling between handlers.

Add a console regression case for sequential task counts and listing. Use
direct Java build and launch commands so the test plan runs in this Windows
workspace without Bash.

The Java sources contain inconsistent spacing, overlong expressions,
ambiguous method names, and incomplete API documentation. These issues make
the code harder to read and conflict with the project-wide SE-EDU standard.

Standardize naming and formatting, document public APIs, encapsulate utility
classes and internal constants, and remove unused code. Preserve all console
messages and application behavior so the cleanup remains low risk.
